writeup.headline: Fastly rates Hold: strong growth, net cash and momentum are offset by a very high valuation and weak profitability.
writeup.thesis: Fastly scores 52, in the middle of the Hold band. Growth is a clear strength (75), with TTM revenue growth of 20.4%, latest-quarter revenue growth of 23.3% year on year, and growth sped up by 3.5 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet (92) shows net cash, and the trend score (79) reflects shares up 199.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, with the price 28.9% above its 200-day average. Weighing against this, valuation scores just 9. In absolute terms the P/S of 6.3x and P/FCF of 86.0x are high, and the FCF yield is 3.8 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. P/S is also more expensive than at 54 of the last 61 month-ends. Quality is weak at 30: the operating margin is -12.0%, stock-based compensation is 19.7% of revenue, and the diluted share count is up 8.1% year on year.
key_risks: Valuation leaves little room for error: P/FCF of 86.0x and an FCF yield 3.8 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield
The company is still loss-making at the operating level, with an operating margin of -12.0%
Heavy stock-based compensation (19.7% of revenue) and dilution, with the diluted share count up 8.1% year on year
After a large run-up the shares are volatile, and the price is 18.3% below its 52-week high
Insider selling by the CEO and CTO, an ongoing securities class action, and meaningful customer concentration
what_would_change: An upgrade to Buy needs 13 more points, for example from operating losses narrowing and dilution slowing, which would lift the quality score
A pullback in the multiples or stronger free cash flow would improve the valuation score from 9
A drop of 8 points would mean Sell, for example if growth slows in the November 4 Q3 results or price momentum reverses
Negative news on guidance, customers or litigation would weigh on the news risk score
